summary: A steel Blaw-Knox lookout in Rothrock State Forest, built 1922; no longer used for fire watch, its first steps removed so it cannot be climbed.

facts.status_note: Still stands, but is no longer used for fire watch, and its first flights of steps have been removed so it cannot be climbed.

access.note: Forest roads and trails in Rothrock State Forest lead to the tower; the tower itself is not open to climbing.

visit.trail_note: A dirt road climbs the ridge to parking about half a mile away (State College); a 2011 account puts parking at the top. The Spruce Gap Trail is the steep hiking route.

events.note: Steel Blaw-Knox tower put into service in the fall of 1922; the 1972 item gives a construction cost of $989.91.
NHLR says the 1922 steel tower replaced an earlier 1915 wood tower. A lookout-history site instead records a 1917 tree observation post 25 feet up.
A November 1972 newspaper item describes someone working on the tower during the fall fire season.
Registered December 31, 2023, nominated by Marc Burns.

corrections.why: The 1972 item quoted on the lookout-history site gives the tower as 55 feet (16.8 m). The record's 18.3 m equals 60 feet, and no Little Flat source read gives 60 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and the 1972 item both support a 1922 steel tower. The earlier structure is disputed: the Register says a 1915 wood tower, the lookout-history site says a 1917 tree platform. The story gives both and does not choose.
The 1972 item says 55 feet, so 16.8 m is used in place of the record's 18.3 m.
The Register gives 2,416 ft and the State College writer gives 2,420 ft. Both are kept as published and the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Main correction: height_m 18.3 to 16.8 (1972 item says 55 ft). The State College article is dated February 14, 2023, so its 'no longer used for fire watch' and 'cannot climb' statements are as of that date. No staffing key is added: the only staffing evidence is a November 1972 note that someone was working on the tower in fire season, with no period given. The 1922 Wilkes-Barre item quoted on the lookout site places the Little Flat tower at Little Flat, Blossburg, which does not match Centre County; not used, probably a different site or a mistake. Parking distance differs between the 2011 account and the State College article; flagged in the story, not resolved. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the earlier note calling the State College article undated was wrong. The story no longer says the tower was in fire-season use in 1972 (the item shows only that someone was working on it), and no longer says mountain bikers use the forest roads. No photos added because credits and licences were not checked.
